Definition: from G3148; to flog (literally or figuratively):--scourge.
BiblicalUsage: mastigóō is to scourge, to flog, and it falls on Christ and on God's children alike. In John 19:1 Pilate takes Jesus and scourges Him, and in Luke 18:33 and Mark 10:34 Jesus foretells that they shall scourge Him and put Him to death, and the third day He shall rise again. In Hebrews 12:6 the Lord scourges every son whom He receives. The word is the whip that chastens and the whip that kills.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mastigóō shows me that the Lord disciplines the sons He receives. I hold that His scourging of Christ is the scourging that saves me.
